1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 3.Bc4 f5.name: King's Gambit Accepted: Bishop's Gambit, Gianutio Gambit
1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 3.Bc4 f5.background: Also called the Nordic Countergambit, it originated in a game between Adolf Anderssen and Louis Eichborn in 1854.

1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 3.Bc4 f5 4.Qe2.strategy: Defends e4 at once, so ...f5 has gained nothing, and leaves the king a square on d1 if the queen checks. White keeps the better development while Black's king is exposed on the e8-h5 diagonal.

1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 3.Bc4 f5 4.Qe2 Qh4+.strategy: Checks at once to rob White of castling, accepting that the queen is exposed. It forces the king to a square it would rarely choose and gives Black time to open the centre with the f-pawn.
